bio: I'm working on building something of my own where Machine Learning meets products that solve real problems and feel effortless to use. I care deeply about the details: how something looks, how it feels, how little it asks of the user. Good systems and **good design**, to me, are inseparable.

Most recently, I built WhiteBox, an AI system designed to act as a financial junior analyst, giving investors everything they need before making a decision: fundamentals, market data, sentiment, and news, all in real-time, orchestrated through specialized sub-agents. It placed 5th at Inter IIT Tech Meet 14.0. I also contributed to **GSoC** 2025 under ML4SCI, submitting a NeurIPS workshop paper as part of the work. As a Research Intern at **NUS**, I explored mechanistic interpretability in LLMs, proposing a novel gradient ascent based approach in sparse autoencoders to extract monosemantic features.

I'm a CSE undergraduate at IIT Dhanbad '27. In the long term, I aim to become an exceptional **ML engineer** and eventually build something of my own. If something meaningful is in the works, I'd love to connect.

agentBio: Daksh Mor is a CSE Undergraduate at IIT Dhanbad ('27) and GATE AIR 362 (Data Science & AI). He specializes in Machine Learning Engineering, Multi-Agent AI Systems, and Quantitative Modeling. Key highlights include: 5th Place at Inter IIT Tech Meet 14.0 (WhiteBox Multi-Agent Engine), GSoC 2025 Contributor at ML4SCI (CERN CMS HCAL Anomaly Detection), NUS Research Intern (Mechanistic Interpretability in LLMs), Kaggle ISIC 2024 Bronze Medal (Top 9%), and 4x National Hackathon Winner.

experiences.summary: Designed & shipped an agentic security VS Code extension combining LLMs with deterministic validation to automate security workflows.
Built a continual learning ViT framework with conv adapters for CERN CMS HCAL anomaly detection, cutting parameters by 60% with zero accuracy loss.
Investigated mechanistic interpretability in LLMs via gradient ascent on sparse autoencoders to isolate monosemantic internal representations.

projects.title: FirstLight - Single-Task macOS App
projects.description: Distraction-free macOS app that sits on your screen and asks one question: "what's next?" Keyboard-only, offline, and stored in plain markdown.

roleBreakdown.sde: Engineered native macOS utility in Swift (AppKit) with LaunchAgent daemon integration for auto-wake on system login and sleep resumption; implemented atomic zero-cloud file I/O continuously synchronizing state to local ~/Desktop/FirstLight/tasks.md with zero external dependencies; packaged for distribution via Homebrew Cask and automated shell installers.
roleBreakdown.ml: Modeled a single-state cognitive task queue eliminating cognitive overload and context switching; structured sequential state persistence to facilitate personal time-series focus analysis and markdown-based task extraction.
roleBreakdown.quant: Formulated chronological event log recording task durations, completion velocities, and timestamped state transitions for deterministic timeline playback and productivity momentum tracking.

roleBreakdown.ml: Developed stroke path vector normalization and generative doodle classification heuristics to parse freehand user inputs into dynamic 3D game props in real time.
roleBreakdown.quant: Designed deterministic state reconciliation algorithms for multi-player collision physics, latency compensation, and 5-round battle royale point aggregation.
